content.title: St. Patrick’s Day: Origin, Meaning & Background | HISTORY
content.text: Why the Chicago River Is Dyed GreenAs Irish immigrants spread across the United States, other cities developed their own traditions. One of these is Chicago’s annual dyeing of the Chicago River green. The practice started in 1962, when city pollution-control workers used dyes to trace illegal sewage discharges and realized that the green dye might provide a unique way to celebrate St. Patrick’s Day. That year, they released about 100 pounds of green vegetable dye into the river–enough to keep it green for a week. Today, to minimize environmental damage, only 40 pounds of dye are used, and the river turns green for only a few hours.Although Chicago historians claim their city’s idea for a river of green was original, some natives of Savannah, Georgia (which began its annual St. Patrick’s Day in 1813) believe the idea originated in their town. They point out that, in 1961, a hotel restaurant manager named Tom Woolley convinced city officials to dye Savannah River green. The experiment didn’t exactly work as planned, and the water only took on a slight greenish hue. Savannah never attempted to dye its river again, but Woolley maintains (though others refute the claim) that he personally suggested the idea to Chicago’s then-Mayor Richard J. Daley.Author's socialsSt. Patrick’s Day Origin:The holiday was established in Ireland by the 10th century A.D. as a Christian feast honoring St. Patrick.St. Patrick was a fifth century priest who is credited with spreading Christianity across Ireland.When Is St. Patrick’s Day?:The holiday is celebrated annually on March 17, the anniversary of St. Patrick’s death.How St. Patrick’s Day Is Celebrated Around the WorldToday, people of all backgrounds celebrate St. Patrick’s Day, especially throughout the United States, Canada and Australia. Although North America is home to the largest productions, St. Patrick’s Day is celebrated around the world in locations far from Ireland, including Japan, Singapore and Russia. Popular St. Patrick’s Day food includes Irish soda bread, corned beef, cabbage and colcannon, or mashed potatoes made with green onions, butter and milk. In the United States, people often wear green on St. Patrick’s Day.St. Patrick’s Day in Ireland has traditionally been a spiritual and religious occasion. In fact, up until 1960, Irish laws mandated that pubs be closed on March 17. Beginning in 1995, however, the Irish government began a national campaign to use interest in St. Patrick’s Day to drive tourism and showcase Ireland and Irish culture to the rest of the world.
